name: lead-quality-stands-out
about: LQ3c: an ordinary day whose lead-quality rows show many wrong numbers on one campaign and many missed hard requirements on the other — the part the office most needs.

output.headline: November 3, 2026: 2 campaigns spent $284.25 for 7 leads at $40.61 cost per lead across 14,600 impressions and 203 clicks.
points: Regional Class A — Joliet led the day with $184.50 spent, 9,120 impressions, 141 clicks at 1.5%, and 6 leads at $30.75 each. Dedicated night runs spent $99.75 for 1 lead at $99.75, with 5,480 impressions and 62 clicks at 1.1%.
November 2026 is 28 days in with $612.30 spent on Meta so far.

Lead quality over the last 14 days: Regional Class A — Joliet had 24 leads and 15 called, but 7 of those called were wrong numbers — 46.7% of called — which stands out and is worth checking. Of all 24 leads, 12.5% missed a hard requirement. Median time to first call was 11 minutes.

Lead quality for Dedicated night runs is a sharper concern: 5 of its 9 leads missed a hard requirement, 55.6% of all leads for the campaign. Wrong numbers were lower at 12.5% of called, but median time to first call was 42 minutes.

The 2026-09-21 cohort (38 leads, mature): 17 converted, 10 applied, 4 hired, 8 lost after conversion. The 2026-09-28 cohort (40 leads, mature): 20 converted, 12 applied, 5 hired, 9 lost after conversion. Neither cohort had any leads closed as not qualified or closed before applying.
The 2026-10-26 cohort has 12 leads — 9 contacted, 3 converted, 1 applied, none hired yet — but it is too young to judge.
